newsitem.title: USA: Western Atlas sees Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: Western Atlas sees Q2 charge.

text.p: Western Atlas Inc Thursday said it expects to take a one-time, non-cash charge of $203 million in the second quarter to write off costs at two units, Norand Corp and United Barcode Industries.
In a statement, the company also said it will expense about $5.0 million in after-tax expenses associated with a planned spinoff later this year.

In May Western Atlas, a technology company with operations in energy-related, manufacturing and automated data collection businesses, said it would spin off its industrial units into separate entities.

"While these one-time charges will impact our second quarter earnings, operational performance in our oilfield services and manufacturing systems businesses during the past three months has continued at a pace comparable to the first quarter," Alton Brann, chief executive, said in a statement.

A company spokesman said based on about 55 million shares outstanding and analysts' expectations, the charge would lead to a second quarter loss of around $3.00 a share. But he noted the research and development being written off is not obsolete and will be used to generate future products.
Analysts had forecast second quarter earnings between $0.65 and $0.72 a share, with a consensus figure of $0.68, according to First Call.
In 1997's first quarter the company earned $0.56 a share based on just over 54.7 million shares outstanding.
Under its spinoff plan, Western Atlas will separate into two publicly traded corporations.

Western Atlas will continue in oilfield information technology, headquartered in Houston, while an as yet unnamed company, based in Beverly Hills, will provide industrial technology products and services for automated data collection, mobile computing and manufacturing systems primarily for automotive and off-road vehicles.
